_comment: IDSA clinical practice guidelines. Source: IDSA 2022/2023 guidelines.
_structure: syndrome → organism → {first_line, dose, duration, notes, alternatives}

K. pneumoniae (susceptible).notes: Standard gram-negative bacteremia. Switch to oral if improving at day 5.

K. pneumoniae (ESBL).notes: ESBL-producing organism. Carbapenems are drug of choice.

K. pneumoniae (CRE).notes: Carbapenem-resistant Enterobacterales. Confirm no MBL before using.

E. coli (susceptible).notes: Preferred agent for gram-negative bacteremia due to susceptible E. coli.

E. coli (ESBL).notes: ESBL E. coli — carbapenems are drug of choice. Meropenem if critically ill.

P. aeruginosa (susceptible).notes: Anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam preferred. Get susceptibilities to guide de-escalation.

S. aureus (MSSA).notes: Anti-staphylococcal penicillin is preferred over vancomycin for MSSA.

S. aureus (MRSA).notes: MRSA bacteremia. Add rifampin only if prosthetic material involved.

Enterococcus (VSE).notes: Ampicillin is preferred for ampicillin-susceptible Enterococcus. Add gentamicin for endocarditis.

Enterococcus (VRE).notes: VRE bacteremia. Daptomycin preferred if high inoculum. Linezolid for VRE faecium.

E. coli (susceptible).notes: First-line for uncomplicated UTI if local resistance <20%. Confirm susceptibility.

K. pneumoniae (susceptible).notes: Oral step-down preferred when susceptible. Ceftriaxone IV for pyelonephritis.

K. pneumoniae (CRE).notes: CRE UTI — systemic therapy required. Confirm KPC vs. MBL genotype.

P. aeruginosa (susceptible).notes: Pseudomonal UTI typically requires anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam.

S. aureus (MRSA).notes: MRSA pneumonia — vancomycin or linezolid. Linezolid may have better lung penetration.

S. aureus (MSSA).notes: Anti-staphylococcal penicillin preferred over vancomycin for MSSA pneumonia.

P. aeruginosa (susceptible).notes: HAP/VAP due to Pseudomonas — anti-pseudomonal beta-lactam. Avoid daptomycin (lung surfactant).

K. pneumoniae (susceptible).notes: CAP-appropriate regimen. Escalate to carbapenem if ESBL suspected.

K. pneumoniae (CRE).notes: CRE pneumonia — ceftazidime-avibactam for KPC. Confirm susceptibility pattern.

E. coli (susceptible).notes: Gram-negative pneumonia — adjust based on susceptibility report.

Enterococcus (VRE).notes: VRE pneumonia — linezolid preferred due to lung penetration.

E. coli (susceptible).notes: Community-onset IAI — covers gram-negatives and anaerobes.

E. coli (ESBL).notes: ESBL IAI — ertapenem preferred over meropenem for non-critical cases (stewardship).

K. pneumoniae (susceptible).notes: Intra-abdominal source. Good coverage of gram-negatives + anaerobes.

K. pneumoniae (CRE).notes: CRE IAI — needs active coverage. Source control critical.

Enterococcus (VSE).notes: Enterococcal IAI — ampicillin-sulbactam covers enterococci + anaerobes.

Enterococcus (VRE).notes: VRE IAI — rare. Ensure source control. Daptomycin alternative.

P. aeruginosa (susceptible).notes: Hospital-acquired IAI or prior antibiotic exposure — cover Pseudomonas.

S. aureus (MRSA).notes: MRSA IAI — uncommon, usually post-surgical. Combine with anaerobic coverage.
